claims.claim_text: The indexed Remsen J Cole is a high-confidence match to the Marine lieutenant colonel named in an official Marines of the OSS roster.
claims.evidence_excerpt: LIEUTENANT COLONELS ... Remsen J. Cole ... Washington
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official Marine Corps history lists the exact rare three-part name among Marine lieutenant colonels who served with OSS, with Washington as his area.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact uncommon first name, surname and middle initial plus explicit OSS context form an exceptionally specific official match despite the index's blank rank and identifier.
claims.temporal_assessment: The roster establishes wartime OSS service and Marine rank but supplies no commission, service-entry or OSS-transfer date.
claims.match_notes: High confidence, not confirmed: the source is an official historical roster rather than a direct personnel-file or service-number linkage, and it describes itself as incomplete.

claims.claim_text: In September 1940, Remsen J Cole headed Remsen J. Cole and Associates, a Philadelphia public-relations consultancy.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Mr. Cole heads Remsen J. Cole and Associates, public relations counsel of Philadelphia.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The contemporary author description identifies Cole as head of the eponymous Philadelphia firm and describes its field as public relations.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact rare three-part name is independently linked to wartime OSS Marine service by the official Marine Corps roster.
claims.temporal_assessment: The role is documented as of 1 September 1940, before wartime OSS service; no service-entry date excludes an intervening role, so it is neither immediate nor last civilian employment.
claims.match_notes: The eponymous firm is modeled as self-employment. The evidence does not establish incorporation, duration, later clients or the date Cole entered the Marine Corps.

person_updates.next_action: Review Box 134 to determine the identifier system and establish Frederic W Cole's full identity, personnel status, occupation, employer and OSS assignment.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The index supplies Nathan L Cole, a short seven-digit identifier, no rank and Box 134. One exact-name Army row exists, but the short value was not padded or assigned to a service-number system to force a match; public results provide no direct OSS bridge.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The exact indexed private identifier selects one of two official Army rows named Raymond T Cole. It dates Army entry to 29 February 1944 as an Air Corps private and carries civilian-occupation code 001.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The exact uncommon Remsen J Cole name in the NARA index is explicitly listed in an official Marine Corps roster of Marine officers who served with OSS during World War II. The roster places him among lieutenant colonels and gives Washington as his service area; it is an official historical compilation rather than a direct personnel-file linkage.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 134 and Marine Corps records to establish commission and OSS dates, test for intervening affiliations after the 1940 firm, and determine the immediate pre-OSS and last civilian roles.
